newsitem.title: POLAND: Four Polish banks initial Pekao merger agreement.
newsitem.headline: Four Polish banks initial Pekao merger agreement.

text.p: Four state-owned commercial banks initialled an agreement on Friday on forming a banking group soon to be consolidated, Bank Pekao SA, the leader of the envisioned banking group, said in a statement.
The other three banks are Powszechny Bank Gospodarczy SA (PBG), Bank Depozytowo-Kredytowy SA (BDK) and Pomorski Bank Kredytowy SA w Szeczinie (PBKS).
"The agreement is initialled and it should be signed by mid-September, after the shareholders of each of the banks approve the signing," Igor Chalupec, a Pekao management board member, told Reuters.

Most likeloy in October Pekao will receive 100 percent stakes in the other three banks with a nominal value of about 100 million zlotys, but the banks' own funds and market value are said to be much larger.
At the end of last year BDK had owned funds of 297 million zlotys, PBKS 257 million zlotys, PBG 200 million zlotys and Pekao 729 million zlotys.
Under the plan, Pekao SA will be privatised following the end of the consolidation process, designed to strengthen the banking sector in the face of international competition.
The banking group will control about 20 percent of Poland's banking service sector.
